t:
Section 2366b(a)(3) of title 10, United States Code, is amended—
    (1) in subparagraph (B), by striking “acquisition cost in” and all that follows through the semicolon, and inserting “life-cycle cost;”; and 
    (2) in subparagraph (D), by striking “funding is” and all that follows through “made,” and inserting “funding is expected to be available to execute the product development and production plan for the program,”.

fable.w: This section only makes technical amendments to the certification criteria in 10 U.S.C. 2366b for major defense acquisition programs, changing the language on life-cycle cost and funding availability. A tempting reading is that an acquisition certification might involve contractors or other outside input, but nothing in the text provides for consultation, comment, hearings, advisory bodies, rulemaking, or a right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government. The certification is an internal Defense Department determination.
fable.s: in subparagraph (D), by striking “funding is” and all that follows through “made,” and inserting “funding is expected to be available to execute the product development and production plan for the program,”.

qwen_block.w: This section is a technical amendment to the United States Code regarding the definition of costs and funding availability for military programs. It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or participation with entities outside the federal government. The text merely changes statutory language related to internal budgeting and cost accounting definitions.

opus.w: This section only changes the wording of criteria in an internal Department of Defense acquisition certification, replacing acquisition cost with life-cycle cost and revising the funding-availability language. It does not involve states, experts, industry, the public or any other party outside the federal government. The procedural setting (a milestone certification) is not enough, because every actor involved is a federal official.

opus.b:
1. **Thinking it through.** One might read this as participation because 10 U.S.C. 2366b covers milestone certification for major defense acquisition programs, a formal procedure before a federal decision. That reading fails. The certification is made inside the Department of Defense. These amendments only change two certification criteria, swapping in "life-cycle cost" and a statement that funding is expected to be available. No one outside the federal government is consulted, and there is no comment period, hearing, rulemaking or right to sue.
